heroHeadline: Colombia's Most Violent Campaign in Decades Ends as May 31 Presidential Vote Approaches
heroSubtitle: Four days from the vote: 61 political leaders killed, 139 municipalities at extreme electoral risk, journalist violence up 175%, and the U.S. threatening to withhold recognition of results. Front-runner Iván Cepeda (left) leads with ~44% in polls, but no candidate is expected to win outright — a June runoff is near-certain, with the future of Total Peace and the 2016 FARC accords hanging in the balance.
footerNote: Data sourced from the Colombian Truth Commission (CEV), JEP, INDEPAZ, InSight Crime, ICRC, Human Rights Watch, UNODC, MOE (Electoral Observation Mission), Ecopetrol, and major international outlets.
